title: Patch: the dungeon run's shop and score strawmen hold run-sim affordability bands
thread:
**Issue #4144 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4144: Patch: the dungeon run's shop and score strawmen hold run-sim affordability bands
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A dungeon run hands out coins and tickets, charges prices at shops and campfires, and turns score into a reward at the end. Many of those numbers are still rough guesses waiting for tuning. Once built, the test suite plays a handful of full runs with the practice opponent and fails when the economy clearly breaks, for example when an ordinary winning run can no longer afford the cheapest shop card, or when the end-of-run reward falls far outside its usual range. Players notice fair shops and meaningful rewards; the maintainer notices the breakage in a test message instead of in player complaints.

## Why

`crates/run/src/config.rs` marks the economy numbers as strawmen "to be tuned": `RUN_COINS`, `RUN_TICKETS`, `RUN_CARD_PRICE`, `RUN_ARTIFACT_PRICE`, `RUN_REMOVE_PRICE`, `RUN_RADIANT_TICKETS`, `RUN_BUFF_TICKETS`, plus the score row (`RUN_SCORE_ROW`, `RUN_SCORE_FIGHT`, `RUN_SCORE_DAMAGE`, `RUN_SCORE_HEALING`, `RUN_SCORE_CARD_DRAWN`, the boss percents, `RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER`) and `RUN_LEVEL_EMBERS`, all specified in `spec/15-dungeon-run.md` §§15.7, 15.8, 15.10 and 15.13. `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs` already prints wins, HP cost, rows reached, score by term and Embers per skill, but its only asserting test is `the_enemy_tiers_hold_run_sims_win_rate_bands` (`BAND_SEEDS = 6`, tier 1 at least 75% won, final boss at most 50% won, elites cost more HP). Nothing asserts the economy, so a price retune that makes shops decoration or Embers noise stays green.

## Proposal

Add an economy-bands test beside the tiers test, reusing its harness (`band_state`, `play_band_fight`/`play_match` at `TEST_BUDGET` and full skill, `KindTally`-style sums over `BAND_SEEDS` runs): tally coins and tickets earned over the first fights, the cheapest shop card, remove and Radiant prices actually charged, and the score-to-Embers payout of finished runs. Fail with a named band break (e.g. "median run cannot afford the cheapest shop card by its first shop" or "Embers per won run outside X..Y") and print the table as `render_bands` does. Keep bands wide because the header warns the AI plays better or worse than a person, so the table guides tuning rather than setting targets; a deliberate retune changes the bands in the same patch, as the tiers test already requires.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs`: new economy bands test and helpers beside `play_bands`, `broken_bands`, `render_bands`
- `crates/run/src/config.rs`: read only (values change only with a deliberate retune)
- SPEC sections read, not changed: §15.7 (packs, coins, tickets, drops), §15.8 (campfire, shop, prices), §15.10 (score and Embers), §15.13 (strawmen to tune); no new ruling since no rules decision changes

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The new test passes on the current strawmen at the same seeds and budget the tiers test uses.
- [ ] Multiplying `RUN_CARD_PRICE` (or zeroing `RUN_COINS`) breaks exactly its band with a message naming the edit, mirroring `each_band_names_the_tier_edit_that_breaks_it`.
- [ ] Pushing score payouts far outside their band (e.g. `RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER` tenfold) breaks exactly its band.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim` stays within a noted time budget, and the daily `run-sim` text output keeps its old rows plus the new economy lines.

## Size and risks

Medium: one tools file plus its tests, no game-rules change. Main risks are flakiness and mistaking AI skill for human value; mitigate with the pinned `BAND_SEEDS` starts, `TEST_BUDGET`, seeded policy order, and wide bands. Rejected alternative: tuning the strawman numbers directly now; rejected because the starting lists are still placeholders (`placeholder.json`, `run_catalog_content`) and the AI baseline is not a human baseline, so bands-that-hold beat numbers-that-guess.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Area: `rules` (`suggestions.areas`).

Class: `checks` → `priority:low`; relabel to change it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-1` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44220008638)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Add a per-PR economy-bands test to `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs`, beside the tiers test and built on the same harness. It fails with a named band break when:

- an ordinary winning run cannot afford the cheapest shop card by its first shop;
- the coins or tickets a run earns, or the Remove, Radiant and buff prices, leave their bands;
- the score or the Embers a run pays leave their bands.

The test prints the table the way `render_bands` does. The daily `run-sim` text keeps every old row and gains economy lines. Synthetic-sample tests, in the style of `each_band_names_the_tier_edit_that_breaks_it`, show which edit breaks which band. No rules decision changes, so no ruling.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs` | `change`. Non-test: `ShopVisit`, `shop_visits`, new `Tally` fields and economy lines in `Tally::render`, and the module-header doc. Test module: economy consts, `EconomySample`, `play_economy`, `broken_economy`, `render_economy` and 3 tests. |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | `change`. Extend the `run-sim` row (line 17): the economy lines, and the per-PR economy bands. |
| `spec/15-dungeon-run.md` | `change`. §15.13, the "Measuring it" paragraph (line 297): add the economy lines and the economy bands after the tier-bands sentence. No ruling. |

Must not touch: `crates/run/**` (config values stay; read only), `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `spec/rulings/`, `spec/pending/`, `spec/11-rulings.md`.

The change is tools-only, so it needs no `cargo jackioh patches` fragment and no catalog change. Governing spec: §15.7, §15.8, §15.10 and §15.13. No existing test breaks, because only lines are appended.

## Steps

1. **Non-test shop reading, in `run_sim.rs`, after `score_parts`.**
   - Add `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] struct ShopVisit { coins: i32, tickets: i32, cheapest_card: Option<i32>, remove: i32, radiant: i32, buff: i32 }`.
   - Add `fn shop_visits(file: &RunFile, content: &RunContent) -> Vec<ShopVisit>`:
     - Start from `run_create(&file.setup, &file.unlocks, content)`; on `Err`, return an empty list.
     - Walk `file.log` with `run_reduce`; on `Err`, stop and return what has been gathered.
     - Record a visit on every step whose new state's phase is `RunPhase::Shop` while the previous state's phase was not. This is the first state of each shop, so a `Buy` inside the shop is not recounted.
     - Fill the visit from `run_shop_prices(&state, content)` (import it from `jackioh_run`):
       - `coins` and `tickets` come from the state.
       - `cheapest_card` is the minimum of `stock_coins[i]` over the `RunShopItem`s whose `good` is `RunShopGood::Card`, `None` if there are none. Import `RunShopGood`.
       - `remove`, `radiant` and `buff` come from `remove_coins`, `radiant_tickets` and `buff_tickets`.
   - These are the prices actually charged, after the relic discount.

2. **`Tally`: new fields.**
   - Add `coins: Vec<i64>` and `tickets: Vec<i64>` (each run's `end.stats.coins_earned` and `tickets_earned`).
   - Add `shops: Vec<ShopVisit>`, all visits of all runs.
   - Add `shop_runs: usize`, the runs with at least one visit.
   - Fill them in `tally()` inside the per-outcome loop: `shop_visits(&outcome.file, content)`.
   - The existing tally tests build outcomes with an empty log, so nothing else changes and they still compile.

3. **`Tally::render`: append after the `Embers:` line.** Do not reorder the old lines.
   - `coins earned: {mean_and_max}` and `tickets earned: {mean_and_max}`.
   - `shops: {shops.len()} visits in {shop_runs} of {runs} runs`.
   - `coins held entering a shop: mean .. (n ..)`, `cheapest shop card: mean ..`, `tickets held entering a shop: mean ..`.
   - `prices: remove {..}, Radiant {..} Tickets, buff {..} Tickets`. Print `-` when there are no shops, using `mean` and `mean_and_max`. Take remove, Radiant and buff from the first visit, or `-`.

4. **Docs in the module header.**
   - Add the economy lines to the "For each skill it prints" paragraph.
   - Add a sentence after the tiers-bands paragraph: "A pull request's tests also hold the economy to wide bands (`ECONOMY_*`)", including how long the test takes (step 8).

5. **Test consts, in the `tests` mod beside `BAND_SEEDS`.**
   - `ECONOMY_RUNS: u32 = 24`. Stub-won runs cost no AI, so 24 is cheap, and `BAND_SEEDS` is a prefix of it.
   - Band consts, each with a doc comment saying what it guards and "(measured: …)".
   - Do not guess the numbers. Measure with the test's printed table (step 7), then set each band wide, as the tiers test does:
     - `*_MIN` is the measured minimum divided by 2 and rounded down;
     - `*_MAX` is the measured maximum times 2.
   - Consts:
     - `COINS_PER_RUN_MIN` and `COINS_PER_RUN_MAX`: the mean coins a won run earns.
     - `TICKETS_PER_RUN_MIN` and `TICKETS_PER_RUN_MAX`.
     - `SCORE_PER_RUN_MIN` and `SCORE_PER_RUN_MAX`: the mean score of an AI run.
     - `EMBERS_PER_RUN_MIN` and `EMBERS_PER_RUN_MAX`: the mean Embers of an AI run. `EMBERS_PER_RUN_MIN` must be at least 1.
     - `SHOP_RUNS_MIN_PERCENT = 50`: the runs that reach a shop.
   - Price bands are relations, not measured:
     - `CARD_PRICE_CEILING_PERCENT` (e.g. 50): the cheapest shop card may cost at most this percent of the mean coins entering a shop.
     - `PRICED_SERVICES_AFFORDABLE`: the median run's total earned Coins covers the cheapest card plus one Remove, and its total earned Tickets cover one Radiant plus one buff.

6. **Test harness, in the `tests` mod after `render_bands`.**
   - **Struct.** `struct EconomySample { runs: usize, coins: Vec<i64>, tickets: Vec<i64>, first_shops: Vec<ShopVisit>, scores: Vec<i64>, embers: Vec<i64> }`.
   - **`fn play_economy(content: &RunContent) -> Result<EconomySample, String>`.**
     - **Stub runs.**
       - `(0..ECONOMY_RUNS).map(|n| play_run(n, content, &Start::default(), &won, None))`. Use the existing `won` stub in the tests mod. Whole winning runs, no AI.
       - Run each with `?`. Any `outcome.faults` makes the result `Err`.
       - Take `coins` and `tickets` from `end.stats`. Take `first_shops` as the first `shop_visits` entry per run, where one exists.
     - **AI runs for score.**
       - Over `0..BAND_SEEDS`, use rayon `into_par_iter`, as `play_bands` does.
       - Call `play_run(n, content, &Start::default(), &|s| play_fight(s, content, AI_SKILL_MAX, TEST_BUDGET), None)`, whole runs, the same seeds and budget as the tiers test.
       - `scores` is `run_score(&end, content)` and `embers` is `run_embers(score)`, one per run.
       - Any fault is an `Err` naming the run.
   - **`fn broken_economy(s: &EconomySample) -> Vec<String>`.** A pure function over the sample, mirroring `broken_bands`. It returns one message per broken band, each ending with the edit that breaks it:
     - "coins earned per won run {mean} outside A..B: RUN_COINS retuned too far".
     - "tickets earned per won run … : RUN_TICKETS".
     - "only {n} of {runs} runs reach a shop, under {SHOP_RUNS_MIN_PERCENT}%": the policy or map no longer gets to a shop.
     - "median run cannot afford the cheapest shop card by its first shop: {coins} held, {price} asked: RUN_CARD_PRICE or RUN_COINS". It compares the median of `coins` entering the first shop against the median of its `cheapest_card`. An empty sample breaks the band.
     - "cheapest shop card costs {p}% of the Coins a run holds entering its first shop, over {CARD_PRICE_CEILING_PERCENT}%": the cards are no longer a real choice.
     - "median run cannot afford a Remove plus the cheapest card over its run: RUN_REMOVE_PRICE".
     - "median run's Tickets cannot pay one Radiant and one buff: RUN_TICKETS, RUN_RADIANT_TICKETS or RUN_BUFF_TICKETS".
     - "score per run {mean} outside A..B: the RUN_SCORE_* row".
     - "Embers per run {mean} outside A..B: RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER".
     - Use integer maths and the medians of sorted copies. A sample with no runs breaks every band.
   - **`fn render_economy(s: &EconomySample) -> String`.** One line per figure: mean and max of coins, tickets, score and Embers, then the first-shop figures. Print them with `mean` and `mean_and_max`, as `render_bands` prints its table.

7. **Tests (see Tests below), then measure and set the bands.**
   - Write the consts with placeholder values first.
   - Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh the_economy_holds_run_sims_bands -- --nocapture`. Temporarily print `render_economy` on success to read the figures. Remove that print before finishing, and print the table only in the failure message.
   - Set the bands as step 5 says and write the measured values in each doc comment, matching the `BAND_SEEDS` comments' style.

8. **Time note.** Time `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim` with `time`. Write the measured wall time next to `BAND_SEEDS` ("the economy test adds about N s"), and say the same in the README row. If the AI runs are far slower than the tiers test, cap them with `max_fights: Some(ECONOMY_AI_FIGHTS)`, set to a number of fights past the first mini-boss. The score and Embers bands are then measured on that cap, and the comment says so.

9. **Docs.** Edit the README row (the economy lines, the economy bands and the time note) and the §15.13 sentence in `spec/15-dungeon-run.md`.

## Tests

All in `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs`, in the `tests` mod.

- **`the_economy_holds_run_sims_bands`**
  - It runs `play_economy` (`.expect("the economy runs end clean")`) and `broken_economy`.
  - It asserts empty with the message "the economy broke its bands (change the bands only with a deliberate retune): … {render_economy}".
  - It must pass on the current strawmen.
- **`each_economy_band_names_the_edit_that_breaks_it`**
  - It builds a `sound` `EconomySample` by hand from plausible measured figures, with the same `with`/edit closure style as the tiers test.
  - Assert `broken_economy(&sound)` is empty.
  - **Card price ×10.** Raise the cheapest-card figure tenfold. Exactly two messages are expected: the "cannot afford the cheapest shop card" one and the ceiling-percent one. Assert each by its `starts_with` or `contains` prefix naming `RUN_CARD_PRICE`.
  - **Zeroed `RUN_COINS`.** Set every `coins` entry and every coins-entering-the-shop figure to 0. Expected: the coins band, the afford band, the ceiling band and the Remove band. Assert those and nothing about tickets or score. The acceptance text says "exactly its band", but zero income cannot avoid breaking affordability, and the plan states this openly. Do not special-case it in `broken_economy`.
  - **`RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER` ×10.** Divide every `embers` entry by 10, leaving `scores` untouched. Exactly one message is expected, containing `RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER`.
  - **Score row ×10 at the same price.** Multiply `scores` and `embers` by 10. Expected: the score band and the Embers band.
  - An edit inside the bands, such as card price ×1.5 or coins ×0.8, breaks nothing.
  - An empty `EconomySample::default()` breaks every band. Derive `Default` for the struct.
- **`the_tally_prints_the_economy_lines_after_the_old_rows`**
  - It builds two outcomes with `RunStats { coins_earned: .., tickets_earned: .. }`. One has a file with a real log that reaches a shop, built by playing `play_run(0, &content, &Start::default(), &won, None)`. The other has an empty log.
  - Assert `tally(..).render("h")` contains `"coins earned: mean "`, `"tickets earned: "`, `"shops: "`, `"cheapest shop card: "` and `"prices: remove "`, all after the `"Embers: "` line (compare `text.find(..)` positions).
  - Assert it still contains `"runs won: "` and `"score from rows: "`.
  - Add one more assertion in the same test: `shop_visits` on a fresh run's empty log returns an empty list, and on the replayed outcome's file returns visits whose `radiant` equals `RUN_RADIANT_TICKETS` and `buff` equals `RUN_BUFF_TICKETS`. If the first stub run has no shop, search `0..ECONOMY_RUNS` for the first run with one.

Commands:

- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh the_economy_holds_run_sims_bands`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh each_economy_band_names_the_edit_that_breaks_it`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh the_tally_prints_the_economy_lines`
- Then `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

To check the acceptance edits in the real code, do both temporarily and revert each: set `RUN_CARD_PRICE`'s Common price to 200, then set `RUN_COINS` to zeros, then set `RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER` to 1000. Confirm the test fails naming the expected bands.

## Done when

- [ ] `the_economy_holds_run_sims_bands` passes on the current strawmen, using the same `BAND_SEEDS` runs and `TEST_BUDGET` as the tiers test for the AI part.
- [ ] The synthetic test shows that a card-price ×10 break, a zero-coins break and a per-Ember ×10 break each name their band. The real-code edits were tried and reverted, and `crates/run/**` is unchanged in the final diff.
- [ ] `run-sim`'s output keeps every old row and gains the economy lines after `Embers:`. `cargo run --release -p jackioh-tools -- run-sim --seeds 2 --budget tiny` shows them.
- [ ] The time added by `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim` is measured and noted in the doc comment and the README row.
- [ ] The README row and the §15.13 sentence are written, and the module header is updated.
- [ ] The harness checks pass: rustfmt, clippy, `cargo test --workspace` (with the testkit and ts features), `cargo jackioh spec check` and `cargo jackioh patches check`. The `spec check` run is a safety check only; no ruling is added.
- [ ] No `#[allow]`, no `#[ignore]` and no lowered band to reach green.

## Risks

- **Flakiness.** All inputs are seeded: the run seed, the policy's own `Rng` stream and the AI at `TEST_BUDGET`. Stub-won runs involve no AI. The bands are 2× wide, and the measured figures sit in their doc comments.
- **Shop reachability.** The random policy may dodge shops in some runs. Hence `ECONOMY_RUNS = 24` and the `SHOP_RUNS_MIN_PERCENT` band. If fewer than half of the 24 runs reach a shop at the pinned seeds, raise `ECONOMY_RUNS` (the runs are cheap), not the policy.
- **Winning stub versus the AI.** Coins and tickets depend on the fight kinds won and on relic passives, not on how the fight was played, so an all-won stub run measures what an ordinary winning run earns. The score and Embers need real reports, so they come from AI runs. A header comment on the bands says the AI plays better or worse than a person, so the bands guide tuning and do not set targets.
- **Test time.** The AI whole runs may be slower than the tiers test; see step 8 for the cap.
- **The pure-crate rule.** `crates/run` stays untouched, and the tools crate may use the disk and clock, though this code uses neither.

## Open questions

None that block the work. The band values come from measurement at the pinned seeds, as the tiers bands did. A person may want the bands narrower once the starting lists leave `placeholder.json`.
```
